 Print Salman Khan dances with his battalion in 'Madirapan' song from 'Maatrubhumi: May War Rest In Peace'; fans compare his moves with 'Jag Ghoomeya' from 'Sultan' and praise his energy at 60 Salman Khan has returned to the dance floor with ‘Madirapan’, a new track from ‘Maatrubhumi: May War Rest In Peace’, and fans are already comparing his moves with ‘Jag Ghoomeya’ from ‘Sultan’. The song shows the actor celebrating with his battalion, with Chitrangda Singh joining in. A lighter side of army life
 While the film is set against a war backdrop, this song takes a relaxed route. Salman Khan is seen sharing drinks, dancing and spending a musical evening with fellow soldiers. Chitrangda Singh joins him for the dance sequences, adding to the festive mood. Watch Salman Khan Makes First Airport Appearance Amid Tiger Shroff Firing Case; Investigation Intensifies Who made ‘Madirapan’?
 Himesh Reshammiya has composed the track, while Sameer Anjaan has penned the lyrics. Mudassar Khan has handled the choreography. It is the latest release from the upcoming war drama. Join conversation
 View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments
 Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines 
 Fans react to Salman Khan’s quirky moves
 Salman Khan’s trademark, slightly offbeat style is back, along with a fresh dance step that has reminded viewers of his earlier hits. Many fans have also been amused and impressed to see him bring such energy to the screen at 60. ‘Maatrubhumi’ gets CBFC nod
 The film has also crossed an important hurdle before release. The Central Board of Film Certification gave it a UA 16+ certificate on November 18, after examining it at the board’s Mumbai regional office. The film was earlier set to arrive on November 20, but it now aims for a theatrical release on December 4, 2026. About ‘Maatrubhumi: May War Rest In Peace’
 Directed by Apporva Lakhia, the film stars Salman Khan and Chitrangda Singh in the lead roles. The movie also features Anoop Bikram Shahi, Mukesh Rishi , Zeyn Shaw, Abhilash Chaudhary, and Ankur Bhatia. It was first announced as ‘Battle of Galwan’ and is based on the 2020 Galwan Valley clash between Indian and Chinese troops. The makers changed the title to ‘Maatrubhumi: May War Rest In Peace’ in March 2026. Poll Vote & Share your view
